recentUsedNativeTickets.head: ce548e5def607ce41459bcc07061861303a8803a
recentUsedNativeTickets.entireOriginalDescription:
Fixes #688

## Cause
`Speed.IsLinear` failed linear work on a slow shared runner because of its absolute 2,000 ms wall-clock cap. Run 42054689905 on #686 timed the Markdown parse at 2,232 ms on windows-latest (`ModelTests.cs:444`), and windows-11-arm has hit 2,169 ms. The parse was linear both times. Only the cap failed it.

## Change
- `Speed.IsLinear` (`tests/AgentBridge.App.Tests/Speed.cs`) now has its own test-local measurer, `Speed.Measure`; it does not use production `Growth`. It times quarter size and full size in turn, takes the median of 3 pairs and judges that ratio against `Speed.MaxRatio` (8×). A slow stretch of the runner now lands on both sizes of a pair, not on one size's block.
- The 200 ms floor and the single remeasure on failure are unchanged from main.
- The absolute 2,000 ms cap is removed. Growth alone decides.
- The Markdown test is renamed `Runs_of_markup_the_parser_is_quadratic_on_are_read_in_linear_time`.

## Proofs
1. **Fake clock (`SpeedTests`):** linear work taking 2.2 s at full size, with one run paused for 30 s, passes. Quadratic work with one paused quarter-size run still fails. Verdict cases at 2,169, 2,232 and 20,000 ms pass for linear growth and fail for quadratic growth.
2. **Real O(n²) mutation (`SpeedQuadraticControlTests`):** the Markdown test's own work (`MarkdownModel.Parse` + `Outline`), with a deliberate quadratic pass added, is measured for real. **CI runs it, and it must fail the check.** The test asserts that `Speed.IsLinear` throws "grew faster than linearly".

## Scope
All callers of `Speed.IsLinear` move to the new check: the 3 tests in `ModelTests`, 1 in `NeedsYouTests` and 1 in `SignInTests` (which calls it twice). Only `ModelTests.cs` (the rename) and `Speed.cs` change.

## Placement
`SpeedQuadraticControlTests` holds a core for seconds. It runs in the existing non-parallel `GrowthTests` collection (`DisableParallelization = true`), alongside Growth's own controls, so it can't skew the other speed tests' timings and they can't skew its.

## Runtime cost
About 5 s extra on x64, about 14 s on Arm.

**Test-only: no production code changes.**

## Grant
Approved by the Head of Engineering on #688 (comment 6664196411), option (c): Platform's #713 is closed and perf-A opens this PR. The helper-wide scope and both proofs are approved. One push, exempt from the cap.

recentUsedNativeTickets.head: 379c41cfcda5063cdda4993a8e5ff1cac58cee53
recentUsedNativeTickets.entireOriginalDescription:
Fixes #901

## Cause
The host can ask a launch's Trust question again under a new id between the launch's outcome and the Trust pressed in the app. `askedBy` (`LaunchViewModel.Trust.cs`) kept only the first question's id, so a Trust that started the agent left the launch's prompt in the box. In the `Following` branch the status became "Session started.", but the prompt stayed, and `late = null` then stopped `StartedLate` from ever clearing it. A prompt left in the box invites a second press, which is what #122 set out to remove.

## Fix
- `askedBy` now keeps the whole `TrustQuestion` and matches it the way `LateStart.Asked` does: by id, or by folder, agent and `AskedAt`. The rule is now one helper, `SameQuestion`, used in both places.
- The `Following` branch clears the launch's unchanged prompt before `late = null`, using the same check as `StartedLate`. A prompt typed since then stays.
- No wording or protocol change.

## Tests (fail before, pass after)
There are two new tests in `TrustTests.cs`. Each one reissues the question as `q-1b`.

| Test | `origin/main` src (96f2426d) | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Trusting_a_followed_launchs_question_asked_again_under_a_new_id_clears_its_prompt` | Failed (`Assert.Equal`: the prompt was still in the box) | Passed |
| `Trusting_an_unfollowed_launchs_question_asked_again_under_a_new_id_clears_its_prompt` | Failed (`TimeoutException` at :330 waiting for "the launch started": the launch stayed unconfirmed; corrected after Engineering's review 6667418472) | Passed |

To see them fail, I checked out `src/AgentBridge.App.Core` from `origin/main` and ran `dotnet test tests/AgentBridge.App.Tests --no-restore -m:1 --filter FullyQualifiedName~asked_again_under_a_new_id`. I then restored the src with `git checkout HEAD -- src` and ran the same command again; both tests passed.

I then ran the whole App test project once, with no filter: 1061 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.

## Review
A code-review agent read `git diff origin/main` locally and found nothing.

Engineering reviews (grant 6664197043).

recentUsedNativeTickets.entireOriginalDescription:
Part of #805
Part of #580
Consumed by #819

## Slice 1, not a second #819 writer
Graceful **process-local** lifecycle coordination only. No scheduler, installer, apply loop, remote command or forced watchdog restart. Draft #815's slice-1/slice-2 note is updated in the same atomic push (docs head `6cdff456916c050a886e6ba5b7ff533228cf2a3a`).

### Shared primitive
- One `DeliveryGate` spans actual answer/reply/attachment injection/stop/launch/folder-trust requests. `OutcomeMemory` takes admission before accepting/scheduling work, not only at the later session claim.
- `LifecycleCoordinator.TryAcquireQuiet(maxWait, DeparturePurpose)` waits <=10 s (default 5), grants a nonrenewable 30 s provisional lease. Quiet now, never whole-session idle or `AutoUpdater.IdleFor`.
- `DepartureConditions.Register(purpose, IDepartureCondition[])` is composition-only, once per purpose and frozen on coordinator creation. Closed `DepartureBlocker` kinds; synchronous snapshot-only conditions, no call-site predicate. `CommitDeparture(lease)` rechecks under the same delivery critical section and evaluates all registered conditions exactly once. Blocking/throwing/reentrant conditions abort; unknown kinds refuse registration. Actual App/other-host/channel/transfer conditions belong to their owners and are NOT implemented. Missing registration fails closed.
- A committed `DepartureGuard` retains the fence until process exit, even if guard/lease is disposed. No guard-release API.
- `AnnouncePlanned` binds the cached receipt to the lease/current connection and enforces a five-second acceptance deadline, including synchronous transport stalls. Default update return is 90 s. Negotiated failure never falls back to Legacy; Legacy is only for independently authorized person restart/stop when capability was not negotiated.
- Abort/release/expiry cancels **after** fence/internal locks release, bounded to five seconds without blocking the next acquisition. `QuietLease.CancellationStatus` / `Cancellation` reports `CancelUnsent` for timeout/failure/unsent cancellation.
- Forced recovery, external-process restart and queued-input handover refuse `JournalUncertain`. No recovered journal or cross-process exclusion is claimed.

### #580/#581 adapters and sensitive publication change
- `ReleaseEligibility.IsHalted`, `IsNewer`, `Evaluate`; numeric canonical `0.1.<run>`, strictly newer, never downgrade.
- One canonical `ops/halts.json`: a valid published empty list means no halts; missing/unreadable/malformed policy is `HaltListUnavailable`, never up to date.
- `GitHubHaltListSource` verifies fixed-repository release asset URL, bounded bytes and SHA-256 digest from GitHub HTTPS metadata. This is verified release metadata, NOT an independent publisher signature/new key.
- Small sensitive change to existing `build/publish-prerelease.ps1`: upload `halts.json` before the release draft becomes public. Mock test proves the ordering. No existing updater is switched to these adapters, and no live policy/release/bootstrap was modified.

## Validation (BelowNormal, one narrow run at a time)
With `AGENT_BRIDGE_NUGET_SOURCE=https://packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io/nuget/v3/index.json`:
- `pwsh quality/run.ps1 -Suite host,host-delivery` after fresh-main rebase: host **737 passed**, host-delivery **235 passed**, ring-0 exclusions intact.
- After announcement deadline review fixes, `pwsh quality/run.ps1 -Suite host`: **739 passed** on final head. Host-delivery source is unchanged from its passing run.
- `pwsh build/test-publish-prerelease.ps1`: **all publisher mocks passed** after rebase; no real release operations.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`: passed.
- A project-local PowerShell forwarding helper added `-m:1 -nr:false`; scratch/runtime files stayed under this worktree's out/. Two initial CMD-helper attempts failed filter forwarding and were replaced; those are not claimed as passing catalog runs. No full ring/solution, load tests, live bridge/hooks/daemon/HA/MQTT operations.

## Review and remaining work
Full static code-review agent review found two announcement-bound bugs; both fixed with focused tests. Final delta review on `0327cc2eabeb4ed83f1b4c3ac735dc806a776b86`: no significant issues. The docs slice note was included in that review. Engineering owns independent sensitive review; no receipt or admission requested.

Before push, #815 had no Connection veto and latest #689 comments had no new push freeze. Main is currently red with **ordinary landing paused**; this draft requests no exception, merge or retry.

Remaining: real relay capability/transport and durable ack validation; owner condition snapshots/registrations and consumer binding; #819/Daily host-only package boundary; Connection's slice-2 journal/cross-process decisions; independent review and normal CI. Existing Serve composition is intentionally unregistered, so no existing departure command can bypass missing owner conditions.
